name: Kenya
genZNote: Kenya's Great Rift Valley is literally where some of the oldest human ancestor fossils have been found — earning East Africa the nickname 'the cradle of humankind' — and it's also where the modern safari and wildlife-conservation tourism model was essentially born.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in East Africa on the Indian Ocean, bordered by Somalia, Ethiopia, South Sudan, Uganda, and Tanzania, and crossed by the Equator.
The Great Rift Valley runs through the country, home to significant fossil discoveries of early human ancestors and diverse wildlife.
Home to Mount Kenya, the second-highest peak in Africa, and extensive savanna grasslands supporting world-famous wildlife reserves (Maasai Mara).

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Swahili and English are both official languages, alongside dozens of indigenous ethnic languages reflecting Kenya's diverse ethnic composition (including Kikuyu, Luo, and Maasai communities).
The Maasai people are internationally recognised for their distinctive traditional dress, culture, and close relationship with wildlife conservation areas.
Kenya has produced some of the world's most successful long-distance runners, a source of major national pride and global sporting recognition.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A presidential republic with a bicameral Parliament, gained independence from British colonial rule in 1963 under founding leader Jomo Kenyatta.
Adopted a new Constitution in 2010 that significantly devolved power to 47 newly created county governments, a major governance reform.
A regional leader in East Africa, hosting the UN's only major headquarters (UNEP and UN-Habitat) located in the Global South, in Nairobi.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: A pioneer in mobile money technology through M-Pesa, one of the world's most successful and widely studied mobile financial inclusion systems.
A significant hub for wildlife conservation science and research, given its globally important national parks and reserves.
Home to Nairobi's growing technology startup ecosystem, sometimes nicknamed the 'Silicon Savannah'.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A regional diplomatic and economic hub for East Africa, hosting UN agency headquarters (UNEP, UN-Habitat) in Nairobi, a rare distinction for a Global South city.
A founding member of the East African Community (EAC), promoting regional economic integration.
An active contributor to regional peacekeeping and mediation efforts across East Africa and the Horn of Africa.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Kenya share a 'Strategic Partnership', with a historically significant Indian-origin community in Kenya dating to railway construction during British colonial rule.
Growing trade, investment, and development cooperation, particularly in pharmaceuticals, IT, and infrastructure.
India has extended lines of credit to Kenya for infrastructure and agricultural development projects.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: East Africa's largest and most diversified economy, strong in agriculture (tea, coffee, horticulture exports), tourism, and financial technology.
A pioneer and global leader in mobile money adoption through M-Pesa, transforming financial inclusion domestically and regionally.
Tourism, centred on wildlife safaris and coastal destinations, is a major source of foreign exchange revenue.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: World-famous wildlife safaris, particularly in the Maasai Mara.
Producing some of the world's greatest long-distance runners.
Pioneering mobile money technology through M-Pesa.
The Great Rift Valley and significant early human fossil discoveries.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Kenyan Shilling (KES).
East Africa's largest economy, driven by agriculture (tea, coffee, horticulture), tourism, and a growing technology/fintech sector.
Nairobi is a major regional financial and tech hub, home to the pioneering mobile-money system M-Pesa.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Home to the Maasai Mara, part of the wider Serengeti ecosystem famous for the annual wildebeest migration.
Mount Kenya, Africa's second-highest peak, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: British colony until achieving independence in 1963 under founding president Jomo Kenyatta.
The Mau Mau uprising in the 1950s was a pivotal independence movement against colonial rule.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1963 independence from Britain; became a republic in 1964.
The 2010 Constitution introduced major reforms, including devolved county governments and an expanded Bill of Rights.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: World-renowned in long-distance running, producing numerous Olympic and marathon champions.
Rich Maasai and Swahili cultural heritage along the coast and interior.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of the African Union; hosts UN-Habitat and UNEP headquarters in Nairobi.
Member of the UN and the Commonwealth of Nations; a key East African regional diplomatic and security hub.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Kenya is an East African presidential republic on the Equator, a regional economic and diplomatic hub known for wildlife tourism, distance running, and mobile money innovation.
keyFacts: Presidential republic; independence from Britain in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta.
2010 Constitution devolved power to 47 county governments.
Pioneered mobile money via M-Pesa; hosts UN agency headquarters (UNEP, UN-Habitat) in Nairobi.
commonConfusion: Kenya hosting UN agency headquarters (UNEP, UN-Habitat) in Nairobi is unusual — most UN headquarters are located in the Global North (New York, Geneva, Vienna).

highYieldFacts: Kenya: presidential republic, independent since 1963; 2010 Constitution devolved power to 47 counties.
Pioneered mobile money (M-Pesa); hosts UNEP/UN-Habitat headquarters in Nairobi.
India-Kenya: Strategic Partnership; historic Indian-origin community from colonial-era railway construction.
commonTraps: Assuming all UN agency headquarters are in developed nations — Nairobi hosts UNEP and UN-Habitat.
Confusing Kenya's 2010 constitutional devolution with full federalism — Kenya remains a unitary state with devolved counties.
mustRemember: Kenya: East African hub, M-Pesa pioneer, hosts UNEP/UN-Habitat, 47 devolved counties, historic Indian diaspora link via railways.
